transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Lakeside CISO), Carlos (Head of IT), Linda (Compliance)

00:00 - Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you all hear me okay?
00:03 - Maya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks.
00:06 - Sofia: Great. Quick agenda — go over our SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture, show where the reports live in the Trust Center, talk mapping between controls, and then dive into specific asks around SSO/RBAC, audit logs, and encryption/KMS.
00:18 - Carlos: Sounds good. We mostly want to confirm whether Redwood's reports map cleanly to our ISO questionnaire and how evidence collection will work for the audit.
00:25 - Ethan: Perfect, that's what we'll focus on. I'll start with a high level of how our compliance artifacts are organized, then get into some technical bits.
00:34 - Ethan: So first, SOC 2 Type II — we have the full report and a summary package in the Trust Center, link I'll share after the call. The standard scope covers production inference, control plane access, and log collection for all hosted tenants.
00:47 - Maya: Is the scope limited to hosted or does it include Dedicated/Private deployments?
00:52 - Ethan: Good question. The Type II report covers our hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated clusters where we operate the control plane. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), we provide a controls bridge and documentation but those are usually scoped separately — customers need to include their deployment in their own audit evidence. The Trust Center has a section that outlines the boundaries.
01:06 - Linda: When you say controls bridge, do you have a mapping doc that shows which Redwood controls meet which ISO 27001 clauses?
01:12 - Ethan: Yes, we maintain a SOC2-to-ISO mapping spreadsheet. It's a template we provide to customers — it shows control IDs, the Redwood evidence artifacts (logs, config snapshots), and suggested customer evidence where applicable. I'll attach a sanitized sample.
01:24 - Carlos: Good. A couple of things we care about: SSO (we use OneLogin), SCIM provisioning, RBAC groups synced from Okta, and KMS integration for key management.
01:33 - Sofia: Great, note taken. Ethan, maybe walk through SSO and KMS at a high level?
01:38 - Ethan: Sure. For SSO we support SAML2.0 and OIDC for enterprise customers, and we can do SCIM for user/group provisioning. RBAC in the Console supports role templates and custom roles; audit events record admin changes, role grants, and API keys creation.
01:54 - Ethan: For KMS, in hosted we default to our managed keys but we also support customer-managed keys in a couple ways — bring-your-own-key via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for encryption at rest of customer artifacts. For Dedicated and Private, customers can point to their own KMS/HSM — that is typical for regulated workloads.
02:10 - Maya: Do you produce key access logs that we can include in the audit evidence?
02:14 - Ethan: We produce operation-level logs (e.g., key usage events proxied through the service) and we can provide guidance for customers to get cryptographic audit logs from their KMS provider. There's a small gap sometimes in mapping vendor-managed key telemetry to application-level audit — we'll show the recommended combo in the mapping doc.
02:28 - Linda: Audit log retention — our policy requires 7 years for certain categories. What is Redwood's default retention and can we request extended retention?
02:36 - Ethan: Default retention is 90 days for the full, hot audit logs in the Console, 365 days for compressed/archived logs in our backend. For long-term retention (multi-year), we offer export to customer-owned S3 buckets or a secure evidence export for Dedicated/Private. We'll include retention options in the package.
02:51 - Carlos: So for long-term logs we'd pull them into our own S3 with encryption and lifecycle rules?
02:56 - Ethan: Exactly — we provide an export job or streaming delivery to your bucket with server-side encryption. For hosted customers we can also configure a secure export with restricted delivery.
03:05 - Maya: Data residency — we process inference in regional clusters. Can you confirm regional boundaries and whether PII is stored/retained in any cross-region caches?
03:14 - Ethan: We have region‑specific serving endpoints. By default, data is processed and stored in the region you select. Prefix/KV caching can appear in the same region; we don't replicate cached KV across regions unless configured as part of a cross-region routing policy. We'll include a region map and the default retention/replication behavior.
03:30 - Maya: Okay, that's helpful. For ISO mapping we also need control owners and where evidence is stored.
03:35 - Ethan: In the mapping spreadsheet each control row has columns: control statement, Redwood artifact, recommended customer artifact, evidence location (e.g., Trust Center link, console export, S3 path). I'll populate those columns in the sample.
03:47 - Carlos: About Trust Center access — is it a public page or a gated portal?
03:51 - Sofia: Trust Center is gated; we can provide a public summary but full artifacts like SOC2 Type II PDF typically require an NDA or portal access. We'll share a link and credentials/one-time link for your audit team.
04:02 - Linda: We'll need the SOC 2 and the Section mapping by next week — auditors want to see mapping to Annex A for ISO.
04:10 - Ethan: We'll make Annex A (ISO) crosswalk entries in the mapping sheet. Quick note — some controls are shared responsibility; we'll mark those clearly so your auditors understand where Lakeside needs to provide evidence (e.g., network segmentation in your VPC).
04:25 - Maya: What's the usual level of detail in the evidence? For example, do auditors expect raw logs or summarized exports?
04:31 - Ethan: Often both — they'll ask for sampled raw logs for specific dates and summaries showing continuous controls. We typically provide packaged evidence: config snapshots, log extracts for samples, and runbooks showing process. For things like SSO provisioning, you'll also provide your IdP logs.
04:45 - Carlos: Is there an interface to query historical admin changes? Our SEC folks like to trace change windows to a particular user.
04:52 - Ethan: Yes — admin audit trails are queryable in the Console; you can filter by event type, user, date range, and export results. We'll show that in the technical walkthrough.
05:02 - Maya: About encryption in transit — do you enforce mTLS between control plane and runtime?
05:07 - Ethan: We use TLS with mutual authentication for internal service-to-service; customer-facing TLS is TLS 1.2+ with HSTS; for Dedicated/private deployments we can enable mTLS on internal links if your security team requires it.
05:18 - Linda: Any SOC 2 exceptions or recent issues we should be aware of?
05:22 - Sofia: Nothing major in the last cycle — there were a few minor control exceptions around patch windows that were documented and remediated. We'll surface the exception write-ups in the report.
05:33 - Maya: For the Trust Center, is there a way to scope what artifacts are visible per customer? We don't want other customers' attachments showing up.
05:40 - Ethan: Artifacts are per customer; we never surface other customers' artifacts. The Trust Center is multi-tenant in UI but artifact access is per contract/portal permission.
05:50 - Carlos: We'll have auditors ask for a sample of your vulnerability scan reports and penetration test summaries. Are those included?
05:57 - Ethan: We include high-level pentest summaries and a penetration testing attestation. Raw pentest reports can be shared under NDA in a secure artifact exchange. Vulnerability scan summaries and patch metrics are included in the SOC 2 controls evidence.
06:10 - Maya: Regarding evidence retention and chain-of-custody, do you time‑stamp evidence exports and provide checksums?
06:17 - Ethan: For exported artifacts we can include checksums (SHA256) and time stamps; for Dedicated/Private we recommend customers pull evidence to their own repository for long-term custody.
06:27 - Linda: One compliance nuance — we need to show segregation of duties for key admin actions. How granular are your RBAC roles?
06:34 - Ethan: RBAC supports read-only, operator, admin, and custom roles. You can separate role privileges so, for example, a billing admin cannot modify runtime clusters. The mapping doc will include which role is expected to perform which activity for evidence.
06:48 - Carlos: Let's talk about backup encryption and key rotation — do you rotate keys automatically or is that customer controlled?
06:54 - Ethan: For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our key rotation policy; for customer‑managed KMS keys, rotation is controlled by the customer KMS; we can show rotation logs as part of evidence where available.
07:06 - Maya: A real concern — how do you handle subpoena/requests for data? Do you have a process and notifications to customers?
07:12 - Sofia: We have a legal process for responding to lawful requests. For hosted data we attempt to notify customers unless legally prohibited. We'll include the policy excerpt in the Trust Center packet.
07:22 - Carlos: Great. Any limitations on the scope of SOC2 that we should be aware of when we present to our auditors?
07:28 - Ethan: The main limitation is for Private on‑prem installs — Redwood's Type II doesn't assert control implementation for code you host yourself. We'll call those out as out-of-scope. Also, any third‑party integrations you configure are usually customer responsibilities.
07:42 - Linda: Can you also include sample evidence collection templates so our compliance folks can start gathering items?
07:46 - Ethan: Yes, we'll include an evidence collection checklist and a mapping template.
07:50 - Sofia: Quick recap before we go into Q&A — we'll share SOC 2 Type II and Trust Center link, Ethan will send the SOC2-to-ISO mapping and evidence templates, Lakeside will provide region/residency reqs and auditor list, and we'll schedule a technical evidence walkthrough.
08:05 - Maya: That works. Quick question from my side — what's the SLA around evidence requests during an active audit? Like if auditors ask for a two-week export, how quickly can you provide it?
08:14 - Ethan: For standard hosted exports we can produce packaged evidence within 3-5 business days; if it's a large historical export it may take longer — we partner with customers on timelines and dedicate support for audit windows. For Dedicated we can often do faster since data paths are isolated.
08:29 - Carlos: Any cost implications for extended retention or export?
08:32 - Sofia: Yes there are typically charges for long-term storage exports or dedicated export jobs; we'll include pricing notes in the follow-up materials.
08:41 - Linda: Okay, no further questions from compliance side.
08:44 - Maya: From ops, once we have the mapping we'll want a walk-through of how to pull specific logs and a dry run.
08:50 - Ethan: We'll set up a 60-minute technical session and demo the Console exports, the API endpoints for audit logs, and an S3 export job.
08:58 - Sofia: Great, I'll send calendar invites for the follow-up. Any last items?
09:03 - Carlos: Minor note — we may want a clause in our contract about support during audit windows.
09:08 - Sofia: Noted; I'll pass to RevOps and Legal.
09:11 - Maya: Thanks, everyone. Looking forward to the materials.
09:15 - Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up. End.
